Independently summed exact Catalan split weights and BST uniform-root split weights for every 2<=n<=59, recovering both covariance expressions including n=2 zero. BST conditional cherry means g(0)=0, g(1)=1, g(t)=(t+1)/3 for t>=2 imply the four exceptional indicator regression and Cov=-8(n-2)/(3n); the stated nonlinear split profile follows directly. Stirling supports the distinct asymptotic orders. These computations corroborate the algebra, not a proof by enumeration.

originality.rationale: Decisively covered. Published November 2 Catalan result contains the EXACT Catalan covariance, asymptotic, and conditional cherry regression. More importantly, October 25 Yule–Harding–Kingman (YHK) theorem states, for N>=10 leaves and UNIFORM root daughter leaf size K, Cov(C_N,g(K))=[g(2)+g(N-2)-g(1)-g(N-1)]/[3(N-1)] for ANY g. A random BST with n internal keys and n+1 external leaves has exactly the corresponding ordered Yule splitting law (uniform root split, recursively independent subtrees); setting N=n+1, K=k+1, and g(K)=(2K-N)^2 immediately gives the submitted BST -8(n-2)/(3n) for n>=9, and its same boundary regression. The remaining n=2..8 values are trivial finite checks. Different nomenclature does not avoid this direct stronger prior theorem.
